The test image shows a close-up of a dark brown, dusty/fuzzy lesion on a green surface (appears to be a tomato fruit or stem). Key features:
- Dense dark brown sporulation with a dusty/powdery texture
- Concentric zonation pattern within the lesion
- Lesion on green plant tissue (likely fruit surface)

Top candidates: Early_Blight (concentric rings, dark brown), Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers (dark Alternaria sporulation on fruit/stem), Gray_Mold (fuzzy sporulation).

**Test image analysis:**
- Macro close-up of a dark brown, granular/dusty sporulation mass
- Clear concentric zonation (ring-within-ring pattern)
- On a green curved surface (unripe tomato fruit)
- Dense, powdery-textured sporulation

**Reference comparison:**
- **Early_Blight**: Leaf lesions showed dark brown centers with yellow halos and concentric rings — the concentric zonation pattern is the hallmark of Alternaria solani. The CDDM image showed dark powdery sporulation on green tissue, partially matching.
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: All references were microscopic images or stem canker, no macro fruit lesion match.
- **Gray_Mold**: White/gray fluffy mycelium — clearly different color and texture.
- **Anthracnose**: Sunken, tan circular lesions on red fruit — different appearance.
- **Late_Blight, Rhizopus, Sclerotinia, TSWV, Septoria**: None match the dark granular sporulation with concentric rings on fruit.

**Conclusion:** The concentric ring/zone pattern with dense dark brown granular sporulation on green fruit tissue is the diagnostic hallmark of Early Blight (Alternaria solani). While reference images I accessed showed primarily leaf symptoms, Early Blight commonly produces identical concentric-zoned lesions with dark sporulation on fruit tissue. No other class in the references produced this distinctive pattern.
